title: ISAC HONOREES
full_story:
The Illinois Student Assistance Commission (ISAC), the state’s college access and financial aid agency, is pleased to announce the 2026-27 Financial Aid Application Completion Recognition of Excellence Honorees.  These Illinois public and private high schools have attained outstanding financial aid application completion rates; demonstrating ongoing support for their students through the financial aid process.  This recognition celebrates each school’s dedication to helping students access financial aid to help them pursue their educational goals.  This year, 539 schools were honored, almost a 15% increase over last year’s honorees.

Locally, The Flora High School was awarded a Silver Medal for a 76% FAFSA completion rate and Clay City High School was awarded a Bronze Medal for a 69% FAFSA completion rate.  In Wayne County, Wayne City and Cisne High School were awarded Gold Medals for 93% and 89% FAFSA completion rates, Fairfield High School was awarded a Silver Medal for an 83% FAFSA completion rate.

The Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA®) is the application that determines eligibility for federal and most state and even institutional financial aid.  The Alternative Application for Illinois Financial Aid, available October 1st for the 2027-28 academic year, offers a way to apply for state financial aid for certain students who are not eligible for federal financial aid.

Illinois requires all public high school seniors to complete either the FAFSA or the Alternative Application as part of graduation requirements.  High schools are expected to provide students and their families with the support or guidance necessary to comply with the requirement, including the opportunity to complete their application during school hours.  For students who choose not to file an application, a parent or guardian can opt-out by completing a simple Financial Aid Application Nonparticipation Form.

Each of the honorees will receive award banners from their local ISACorps member to display at their school.

title: CHILD SAFETY SEAT INSPECTIONS
full_story:
Tomorrow the Clay County Health Department will be offering Car Seat Safety checks from Noon until 4 pm.

During this time certified child passenger safety technicians will provide a free car seat safety check.  Is your car seat expired, installed correctly or is it the right seat for your child.  Find out for free and get any questions answered.

Illinois recognizes Child Passenger Safety Week September 20th through 26th, to remind parents and caregivers that state law requires children to ride in a child safety seat until age 8 and rear-facing until age 2.  During this time certified child passenger safety technicians provide free car seat safety checks throughout the state as part of Child Passenger Safety Week.

According to statistics 3 out of every 4 Child Safety Seats are installed incorrectly.

full_story:

title: MEDICARE OPEN ENROLLMENT
full_story:
Christopher Rural Health Planning Corp. (CRHPC) is reminding individuals age 65 and older that Medicare open enrollment will run from October 15th, through December 7th.  This annual period is when individuals with Medicare can review and change their health and prescription drug coverage for the upcoming year.  It’s also a time for those who turned 65 to sign up for Medicare if they haven’t already done so.

Leading up to the enrollment start date is a good time to review current coverage, preview plan choices, and to review Annual Notices of Change (ANOC).  The October 15th through December 7th time frame is for signing up, switching, or dropping plans.  CRHPC highlights the importance of being informed and knowing that help is available.

Those with questions about plans or in need of assistance navigating Medicare open enrollment are encouraged to contact their local Senior Health Insurance Program (SHIP) counselor at CRHPC by calling 1-833-209-0498.  Whether someone is a CRHPC patient or not, their certified team of SHIP counselors are available to help with reviewing and exploring health and prescription drug coverage options at no cost.  Additional resources and information regarding Medicare open enrollment can be found at medicare.gov and shiphelp.org.

title: IMA LEGISLATOR REPORT CARD
full_story:
With a consistent voting record supporting Illinois manufacturers and the state’s business community, State Senator Jason Plummer earned a 90% rating on the Illinois Manufacturers’ Association’s (IMA) 2025-2026 Legislator Report Card, ranking him among the top lawmakers in the Senate.

“Manufacturers are creating jobs, investing in our communities and helping drive our economy, but too often they are forced to deal with higher costs, unnecessary regulations and mandates that make it harder to compete with our neighbors,” said Senator Plummer.  “I’m proud to be a voice for the employers and job creators who keep Illinois moving, and I’ll continue fighting to make this a state where businesses have the opportunity to grow and succeed.”

The IMA Legislator Report Card examines lawmakers’ votes on key issues affecting Illinois’ manufacturing economy and broader business climate.  Among the issues considered are tax policy, workplace regulations, environmental mandates, energy costs and other policies that can influence businesses’ decisions to invest, expand and create jobs in Illinois.

“Manufacturing is the bedrock of Illinois’ economy, and we’re proud to recognize the elected officials who support policies that allow the industry to grow and thrive,” said Donovan Griffith, Executive Vice President and Chief Strategy Officer of the IMA.

title: ISP ACE PATROLS
full_story:
Illinois State Police Troop 9 Commander, Bruce Waggoner, announced that the ISP will be conducting Alcohol Countermeasure Enforcement (ACE) Patrols in Clay, Marion, Effingham, Wayne Lawrence, and White Counties during October.  Ace patrols allow the ISP to focus on preventing, detecting, and taking enforcement action in response to violations associated with impaired driving and illegal transportation or consumption of alcohol or drugs.

The ISP has zero tolerance for impaired driving in Illinois. Officers working the detail will be watchful for motorists who show signs of impaired driving, operating vehicles in an unsafe manner, driving with a suspended or revoked driver’s license, and transporting open alcoholic beverages, as well as improper seatbelt and child restraint usage, distracted driving, and other Illinois Vehicle Code violations.

Alcohol and drug impairment are estimated to be a factor in more than 47% of all fatal motor vehicle crashes in Illinois.  There is one alcohol-related traffic fatality every 39 minutes in the United States.  The ACE program allows officers to work even harder at removing dangerous DUI offenders from the road.  This project is funded through the Illinois Department of Transportation.

title: NASS LAUNCHES AGINSIGHTS
full_story:
USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) recently launched AgInsights, a new data dissemination tool that will serve as a key component of NASS’s ongoing modernization strategy.

Designed to enhance currently used data products and services, the AgInsights application offers streamlined information dissemination, increased operational efficiency and a more dynamic, interactive experience so producers have easier navigation and access to the latest agricultural data.

NASS recognizes farmers need timely, actionable information to make informed decisions.  AgInsights will bridge the digital divide, ensuring equitable access to critical data for all producers, including those who have historically faced barriers to information.

“AgInsights is an important step forward in how producers interact with agricultural statistics.  By streamlining information delivery and integrating advanced technologies, we’re making it easier for producers to access, analyze, and apply the latest data to their operations,” said NASS Administrator Joseph Parsons.

NASS asked an initial group of agricultural data users to test the application and provide feedback.  Their recommendations informed the development of the product to help meet industry expectations across commodity sectors.

Key features include the integration of tabular data, charts and maps into a single web-based interface, providing a comprehensive and interactive way to explore data, which was previously spread across different formats.  Users can access comprehensive tabular data views similar to traditional PDF reports, but with added interactivity, making it easier to analyze and compare data.

Information about all NASS surveys and reports is available online at nass.usda.gov.
